after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Find an equation of the plane that passes through the point $Q(-2,2,0)$ and is perpendicular to the line 

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=3-4t \\ y=1+6t \\ z=-1+2t.\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
Note that the position vector of $Q$ is $q=⟨-2,2,0⟩.$ Converting the parametric equations of the line to vector form, we get

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=3-4t \\ y=1+6t \\ z=-1+2t\end{aligned}\,⟹\,⟨x,y,z⟩=⟨3,1,-1⟩+t\text{ }{{⟨-4,6,2⟩}_{⏟}}_{v}.
$$

 

The direction vector of the line is $v=⟨-4,6,2⟩,$ so a normal vector to the plane is 

$$
n=v=⟨-4,6,2⟩.
$$

Therefore, the equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-q)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-q\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =q\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨-4,6,2⟩ & =⟨-2,2,0⟩\cdot ⟨-4,6,2⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨-4,6,2⟩ & =20.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

after.problem: A nonzero vector $⟨0,\,b,\,c⟩$ is parallel to the plane $r\cdot ⟨1,2,-1⟩=7.$ What is the value of $\frac{b}{c}?$
after.worked_solution:
We need a vector $v=⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩$ that is parallel to the given plane. 

From the equation $r\cdot ⟨1,2,-1⟩=7$ of the plane, we get the normal vector $n=⟨1,2,-1⟩.$ So, $v⊥n$ and we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot n & =0 \\ ⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩\cdot ⟨1,2,-1⟩ & =0 \\ {t}_{1}+2{t}_{2}-{t}_{3} & =0 \\ {t}_{3} & ={t}_{1}+2{t}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we obtain 

$$
v=⟨{t}_{1},\,{t}_{2},\,{t}_{1}+2{t}_{2}⟩,
$$

where ${t}_{1},{t}_{2}\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

We are told that the first component of $v$ equals $0.$ So, we must set ${t}_{1}=0.$ 

Since $v$ is nonzero, we can pick any ${t}_{2}\ne 0.$ For example, setting ${t}_{2}=1$, we get

$$
v=⟨0,\,1,\,2⟩.
$$

Therefore, $\frac{b}{c}=\frac{1}{2}.$

after.name: Question 3
after.problem: A nonzero vector $⟨0,\,b,c⟩$ is parallel to the plane $r\cdot ⟨-2,2,-4⟩=15.$ What is the value of $\frac{b}{c}?$
after.worked_solution:
We need a vector $v=⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩$ that is parallel to the given plane. 

From the equation $r\cdot ⟨-2,2,-4⟩=15$ of the plane, we get the normal vector $n=⟨-2,2,-4⟩.$ So, $v⊥n$ and we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot n & =0 \\ ⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩\cdot ⟨-2,2,-4⟩ & =0 \\ -2{t}_{1}+2{t}_{2}-4{t}_{3} & =0 \\ 2{t}_{2} & =2{t}_{1}+4{t}_{3} \\ {t}_{2} & ={t}_{1}+2{t}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we obtain 

$$
v=⟨{t}_{1},\,{t}_{1}+2{t}_{3},\,{t}_{3}⟩,
$$

where ${t}_{1},{t}_{3}\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

We are told that the first component of $v$ equals $0.$ So, we must set ${t}_{1}=0.$ 

Since $v$ is nonzero, we can pick any ${t}_{3}\ne 0.$ For example, setting ${t}_{3}=1$, we get

$$
v=⟨0,\,2,\,1⟩.
$$

Therefore, $\frac{b}{c}=2.$

content.problem: A nonzero vector $⟨0,\,b,\,c⟩$ is parallel to the plane $r\cdot ⟨3,2,-1⟩=\sqrt{2}.$ What is the value of $\frac{b}{c}?$
content.worked_solution:
We need a vector $v=⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩$ that is parallel to the given plane. 

From the equation $r\cdot ⟨3,2,-1⟩=\sqrt{2}$ of the plane, we get the normal vector $n=⟨3,2,-1⟩.$ So, $v⊥n$ and we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot n & =0 \\ ⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩\cdot ⟨3,2,-1⟩ & =0 \\ 3{t}_{1}+2{t}_{2}-{t}_{3} & =0 \\ {t}_{3} & =3{t}_{1}+2{t}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we obtain 

$$
v=⟨{t}_{1},\,{t}_{2},\,3{t}_{1}+2{t}_{2}⟩,
$$

where ${t}_{1},{t}_{2}\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

We are told that the first component of $v$ equals $0.$ So, we must set ${t}_{1}=0.$ 

Since $v$ is nonzero, we can pick any ${t}_{2}\ne 0.$ For example, setting ${t}_{2}=1$, we get

$$
v=⟨0,\,1,\,2⟩.
$$

Therefore, $\frac{b}{c}=\frac{1}{2}.$

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=5-3t \\ y=2+4t \\ z=-3+t.\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
Note that the position vector of $Q$ is $q=⟨-1,1,2⟩.$ Converting the parametric equations of the line to vector form, we get

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=5-3t \\ y=2+4t \\ z=-3+t\end{aligned}\,⟹\,⟨x,y,z⟩=⟨5,2,-3⟩+t\text{ }{{⟨-3,4,1⟩}_{⏟}}_{v}.
$$

 

The direction vector of the line is $v=⟨-3,4,1⟩,$ so a normal vector to the plane is 

$$
n=v=⟨-3,4,1⟩.
$$

Therefore, the equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-q)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-q\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =q\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨-3,4,1⟩ & =⟨-1,1,2⟩\cdot ⟨-3,4,1⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨-3,4,1⟩ & =9.\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem:
Find an equation of the plane that passes through the point $Q(-1,1,2)$ and is perpendicular to the line 

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=5-3t \\ y=2+4t \\ z=-3+t.\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
Note that the position vector of $Q$ is $q=⟨-1,1,2⟩.$ Converting the parametric equations of the line to vector form, we get

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=5-3t \\ y=2+4t \\ z=-3+t\end{aligned}\,⟹\,⟨x,y,z⟩=⟨5,2,-3⟩+t\text{ }{{⟨-3,4,1⟩}_{⏟}}_{v}.
$$

 

The direction vector of the line is $v=⟨-3,4,1⟩,$ so a normal vector to the plane is 

$$
n=v=⟨-3,4,1⟩.
$$

Therefore, the equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-q)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-q\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =q\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨-3,4,1⟩ & =⟨-1,1,2⟩\cdot ⟨-3,4,1⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨-3,4,1⟩ & =9.\end{aligned}
$$
